description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §4.3.4's NAME-BASED operand alignment in an array-level equation, and for the scope boundary that rule has. An operand of a bare array-level expression aligns to the result by INDEX-SET NAME: it supplies the axes it is declared over, replicates along the ones it is not, and TRANSPOSES when its declaration order differs from the result's. An operand whose shape is ANONYMOUS — a `faq` result, whose axes carry node-local output symbols rather than index-set names — stays POSITIONAL, and the `broadcast` node spelling is governed by exactly the same rule as the bare one. Every binding got the alignment half wrong in its own vocabulary and in OPPOSITE directions (EarthSciML/EarthSciAST#100): Rust flattened the operand into the result's linear layout and zero-filled the tail, Python right-aligned the way NumPy does, and both produced finite, plausible, wrong fields. A one-operand `broadcast` separately dropped its `fn` and behaved as the identity (#101), which turns a negated flux into an un-negated one — also finite and plausible. The fixtures are documents that carry their own §6.6 `tests` blocks, so the authored expectation travels with the physics; the goldens are the Julia `interpreter`'s actuals for the same assertions.

scope_excluded.go: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so a tier that DRIVES one cannot be run here (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles). This is an exclusion from the CATEGORY, not from the rule.

tolerances.detail: The band between a producer's actual and the Julia-interpreter golden. It is separate from, and tighter than, each assertion's own §6.6.4 band: the assertion states what the PHYSICS is (and is gated at the document's own tolerance by each binding's §6.6.3 predicate), while this states how far two evaluations of the same arithmetic may drift. Every fixture here integrates a CONSTANT tendency from a zero initial condition, or a scalar exponential, so an integrator contributes nothing near this floor.

named_exclusions.reason: Rust's `native` compiler has no wholesale lowering for the array-level `broadcast` node: the build refuses with `compiler_refused_rule` — "compiler 'native' cannot run the continuous-cadence state derivative 'D(dp[1,1,1])': wholesale: unsupported op `broadcast`" — and, being strict (esm-libraries-spec §2.5.10), declines rather than demoting the rule to the per-cell oracle. Measured 2026-09-22 on compiler/testmig at 25efca83a. Rust's own `tests/array_level_broadcast.rs` already forced `Compiler::Interpreter` for exactly this reason; this ledger is the first place the refusal is NAMED rather than worked around. `interpreter` runs the fixture and is required.
